DISCUSSION ITEM a.
Review of Enacted State Budget Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance The Finance and Facilities Committee reviewed the FY27 state budget approved by the General Assembly on June 9, 2026.
Vice President Abby Benson reported that the General Assembly approved a $4.2 million increase to the operating budget, an amount in line with the Governor’s Recommended Budget (GRB), but well below the University’s request of $37.6 million.
She reminded the Committee of the three categories for the request: Operating Budget Shortfall, Current Service Level, and Strategic Initiatives, of which only the Current Service Level was funded.
She noted that of the $4.2 million increase in the operating budget, $1.3 million of this amount reflects support for corresponding expenses imposed by the state for centralized services.
Strategic Initiatives have not been funded for a number of years, but the University continues to maintain this request to signal the importance of these initiatives.

Vice President Benson also noted that the University received $15.2 million for general asset protection, $1.6 million for a campus access control pilot program (to determine the system of record for access control at RI), $8.0 million in RICAP ADA project support and also $18.0 million in RICAP Building Envelope work.
The Capital Improvement Plan included a GO Bond request for $165.7 million for the Integrated Health Building, with the legislature supporting the project at $165.0 million.
The bill also included Kushner authorization for URI to issue revenue bonds for Repaving and Hardscaping ($20.0 million) and Automotive and Administrative Services ($14.4 million).
The enacted budget included $5.0 million for medical school startup funds (operating).
Additionally, the full-time equivalent (FTE) cap was increased by 200 with a new auxiliary cap of 450 FTEs, inclusive of the total FTE count.
Committee members had no questions on the approved budget. 3.

The CIP is a rolling five-year plan submitted to the Board in April for its review and then in June for approval before being submitted to the state.
Vice President Benson noted that the presentation today focused on the changes to the CIP since the April review.
The plan includes $17.8 million for asset protection (RICAP), and two new projects on the Narragansett Bay campus totaling $16.8 million.

BFA Film - BFA The Major.
The BFA in Film/Media is an intensive, experiential degree that integrates advanced creative practice with critical and historical study.
The curriculum emphasizes sequential training in film and media production alongside rigorous engagement with theory, research, and analysis.
Students develop technical and conceptual proficiency through sustained coursework, collaborative projects, and advanced culminating work that reflects professional standards and disciplined artistic inquiry.
FLM 496 (Capstone Seminar in Film/Media) and FLM 397 (1 Credit) BFA portfolio are required in the junior year; and FLM 497 (BFA Capstone) is required in the senior year.
Students learn to work with the evolving and overlapping technologies involved in the production of moving images.
A wide range of courses is available to the Film/Media student—courses that examine the historical, theoretical, and global approaches to the analysis and creation of moving images.
The Film/Media program prepares students for careers in such areas as independent filmmaking; animation and media design; film and television industries, advertising, marketing, public relations, and media criticism.

Graduates of this program are also prepared to continue with graduate studies in film and media production for an M.F.A.
Students majoring in the Film BFA must complete a minimum of 52 credits (maximum 67) in approved courses toward the major.
FLM 101 or FLM 101H is a required prerequisite.
We recommend that students take at least one film production course per semester beginning with FLM 110 in their freshman year, establishing a regular and consistent creative process.
The wide range of choices in Film/Media courses permits students to design a major that will meet both personal and professional goals.
Students must have a plan of study approved by an academic advisor in the Film/Media program before beginning their coursework in the major.

BACKGROUND The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated and qualified vendor to provide emergency and routine utility maintenance and repair services for all underground and above -ground utility systems , excluding electrical , located on the Kingston, Narragansett Bay and W.
Alton Jones campuses .
These critical systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water, natural gas, propane and heating oil.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
URI owned utility systems on the Kingston campus include a central steam plant, steam and condensate distribution/return network s, Five natural gas distribution networks, sewer collection system with four sewer pump stations, potable water supply and distribution, oil and propane fuel storage tanks for heating systems and a stormwater collection system.
The 153 acre Narragansett Bay Campus consists of 41 buildings and 326,000 square feet.

Utilities include natural gas supplied by RIE and distributed by URI owned piping network, potable water provided by the town and distributed by URI owned piping network, sewer collected by URI owned piping network and sent to the town for treatment, stormwater collection sy stem and oil and propane fuel storage for heating and generators.
The W.
Alton Jones campus is a rural campus in West Greenwich, RI and composed of 30 buildings.
Utilities include three small public water systems, septic systems, propane and oil storage for heating systems.
The selected vendor must have a thorough understanding of connection and repair methods for each of these utilities and an integral understanding of each of the university’s utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section B of this solicitation.
The vendor shall demonstrate troubleshooting of utility outages and methods of providing control of the utility network and temporary service.
As such, the selected vendor(s) will be required to study and understand the universi ty’s utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract’s award date.

The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide routine and emergency service for pipefitter, steamfitter and plumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
